\paragraph{HybridMamba.}
At the Mamba~1 budget, the three HM mixtures with dynamic rows exceed all three Mamba baselines on medium and hard. On medium, the complex-dynamic mix has the highest mean of all configurations, $96.9$ [$96.5$--$97.2$]; on hard, the mixtures reach $79.6$--$80.7$, the best within $1.9$ points of the best SSD-MIMO configuration.
The gains build up from Mamba~1’s static design. With the same static per-coordinate decay, HM's maps, two-endpoint write and head organization raise the hard mean from $69.6$ to $79.2$; dynamic rows add $1.4$ points on hard and $2.3$ on medium; complex dynamic rows add a further $3.4$ on medium and are neutral on hard. Complex rows with only static decay hurt on hard ($69.0$). Each step changes several settings at once, so the steps are not isolated mechanisms.
